newsitem.title: GERMANY: German, French socialists want European jobs pact.
newsitem.headline: German, French socialists want European jobs pact.

text.p: French Socialist leader Lionel Jospin and his German counterpart, Social Democrat (SDP) chief Oskar Lafontaine, on Wednesday urged the creation of a European "employment pact" to reduce joblessness.
In a joint statement, the two said Europe's monetary union could only benefit its citizens if accompanied by concrete measures to reduce the current 18 million unemployed across the continent.

They called on the European Council of Ministers to include employment targets within "the front line of its decision-making" and for a specific chapter on jobs policy to be included in the Maastricht Treaty.

They called for increased training opportunities and a requirement on trade unions and employers that wage and employment policies be focussed on ways to create more jobs through the use of productivity gains.
Corporate taxes should be harmonised across the continent to prevent so-called "tax-dumping", where employers flock to those countries with the most favourable tax regimes, they said.
"Monetary union is no end in itself. The euro will only meet with the approval of Europe's citizens if currency union promotes growth, employment and stability in all member states," they concluded.
